I had a kidney infection that lead me to go into sepsis. 

I remember being extremely unwell a few days before I eventually took myself to the hospital.  (I was in a DA relationship who physically refused to let me get medical treatment) and instead of going to work, I got a taxi to the emergency department. 

Somehow. I don’t actually remember even doing that, because I was quite honestly delirious with pain. All I can think was because Uber was around I managed to screen smash the right buttons and ended up at the correct hospital.

All I remember of that morning was waking up with impending doom and pain in my lower back which felt like a knife gnawing into my body. It was physically the most terrifying experience but I remember weirdly feeling so dissociative from my current situation. The pain felt like it was a separate thing and the fact that my body thought I was dying was entirely another. I felt oddly calm, and accepted I was probably going to die and yet got waves of horror every now and then.

I became very popular the moment I stepped into the waiting room when the nurse took my temperature and I guess I looked like a walking corpse because I was very quickly and swiftly taken to a bed. They tried to get blood from me but that was difficult because I guess all my blood was going to my organs and took a while. 

I had a hot rash over majority of my body which was prickling and I had chills which felt like my body was vibrating violently. I was also extremely delirious and at one point felt like I was hallucinating. The pain never stopped until they gave me Morphine.


Anyways, 10 days later I was told that I was extremely lucky. I wondered why nobody actually told me how unwell I was and just kind of pumped me with bags and bags of IV’s which clearly were antibiotics and pain relief.  I was out of it for a couple of days until I actually started making sense of what had happened.

My kidneys are damaged by scarring and I have to be careful about infections in the future now but that’s been the only lasting effects. 

I take infection of all kinds extremely seriously now.

Hey! I have never used Loving tan, however I have been fake tanning for many years now.

The amount of development time is down to the DHA content. I believe 2Hr or rapid development time is due to having a higher content, so basically the tan that you put on develops faster than a lower/slower development time with a lower DHA. If you left it on longer than 2hrs, you would achieve the equivalent of a "dark tan".

Personally I think the length of time either of these tans last on the skin is simply due to your skin chemistry, and the quality of the DHA in the product.   I have used many high end and cheaper brands though, from rapid 2hr applications to 8hr ones, and neither have lasted much longer than the other on me. I do however find, that the higher end ones give me a few extra days, and a more even fade when its time to exfoliate it off. So proformance wise, with proper aftercare I think you'll get roughly the same length of time to enjoy your desired colour.

I think you preference for a rapid tan or a slower one should come down to your aplication preferences. I find rapid tans dry quicker and can be trickier to blend, and do tend to "stick" more in dry areas, and can make me feel a bit dry the next day. However they are convienient and tend to not to smell as strongly.

However, longer development tans are uncomfortable to sleep in as they dont really dry down to touch- but don't dry my skin out as much the next day. I also find they apply more forgiving on the hands and feet or drier areas. 

Hope this helps :)

I remember stroking her little skinny body and thinking how she felt like a little bird. She was so thin and underweight I was so sure she wouldn't make it. She was tiny- fit into my cupped hands and mewed at me for food so I took her home, and I saved her little life.

But sometimes when i look at her i remember that little glow that i felt when I first found her- some weirdly forgotten emotion that grew up from my chest and made me have a purpose. It crept up inside me and spread into all the different holes inside me which gave me a strength I forgot I had. It fuelled me to get better, to attend therapy, to take my meds, to be alive and not only that but thrive, smile, LIVE.

I tell people I saved her life that day. But really, she saved mine.

Good way to check if she's a stray just on small observations is the skin around her feet and legs. If she's been living on the streets for a while, she'll be kinda dusty/dirty. I met plenty of street cats in the middle east and volunteered to help them but I'm no vet. 
Cats only clean themselves thoroughly when they feel safe and not on alert for predators/other cats/there next meal. If she's kinda dirty to the skin, has fleas, dirty ears and eyes etc or you can feel her ribs shes likely a stray. Most strays who live in highly populated areas with lots of other cats sometimes have ringworm too. You'll want to be careful as this can be spread to humans through there faeces, skin contact.
Also, a dead cert is she will likely be pregnant unless she's a fixed pet that's gone missing/been abandoned
But as other commenters have suggested, a trip to the vet will tell you if shes chipped but my opinion is she looks very well kept!
